A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LanDiff research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LanDiff benchmark results, tokenizer and guidance ablations, reconstruction-loss trajectories, and generated-video examples.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including short- and long-video evaluations and the ablations in Table 5.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the Theia-based semantic tokenizer, autoregressive language model, diffusion control module, and chunk-wise streaming procedure. The architecture, losses, training procedures, and inference mechanisms in Section 2 and Appendix A are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use the same 200M video-text training pairs for tokenization and language modeling, 3M high-quality pairs for diffusion, and VBench/VBench-Long evaluation coverage. The qualitative scenarios are retained. v3's proposed image-to-video and interactive extensions are future work.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 3, 4, 5, and 8 and the qualitative comparisons. This includes the controlled DiT and ARLON comparisons, CogVideoX examples, and MagViT2 reconstruction comparisons. Keling becoming Kling corrects naming.

E3.justification: The stated data filtering, 480x720 resolution, 8 fps processing, model configurations, guidance settings, evaluation metrics, and controlled comparisons remain unchanged. Figure 9's revised normalization affects visualization, not the benchmark evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The tokenizer and classifier-free-guidance ablations, IFrame/PFrame loss comparison, and qualitative cases are retained. The added tradeoff and limitation discussion introduces no new ablation, robustness test, or supporting case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the comparisons. The retained raw and smoothed training-loss curves do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 3-5 and 8 retain identical scores. Section 3.2 removes the inconsistent 85.42 prose value, while Table 3 gives 85.43 in both versions, and corrects the quality ranking from second-highest to highest. v3 also states approximate stability gaps in Appendix B and explicitly reports text-rendering difficulty in Section 7.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1-6 are unchanged; neither version adds theoretical results or proofs. The new min-max formula explains Figure 9's display scaling rather than introducing new theoretical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same hybrid-generation contribution, approximately 14,000-fold compression claim, 5B model characterization, and short- and long-video performance claims. Naming and body-text corrections do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v1 mainly interprets successful results and acknowledges small reconstruction discrepancies. v3 substantially expands limitations in Section 7: language-model scale, dependence on CogVideoX-2B, and inaccurate text rendering with a proposed supervision-based explanation. Appendix B additionally interprets short-video performance through the tradeoff between dynamism and temporal stability.

D1.justification: v3 adds a repository link on the title page and explicitly summarizes 3B trainable versus 5B total parameters in Table 7, consistent with v1's module breakdown. Other implementation details remain unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish what the linked repository provides.

R1.justification: The reference list and substantive positioning against prior tokenizers, autoregressive generators, diffusion models, and ARLON are unchanged. Restoring the SAM name beside its existing citation and reformatting related-work headings do not add prior work.

P1.justification: v3 adds Broader Impact and Limitation and Future Works sections, promotes former Appendix A.4/A.5 to Appendices B/C, and converts related-work subsections to paragraph headings. Terminology and result prose receive local corrections; most existing prose and the central narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Existing figures and tables are rearranged and resized, with Figures 5 and 6 exchanging numbering. Figure 9 is redrawn with explicitly documented 0.3-0.8 normalization, Table 7 gains a trainable-parameter row, and schematic labels are adjusted. The displayed video examples and benchmark table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency through explicit limitations, clearer parameter and repository documentation, and disclosure of Figure 9's normalization. It also resolves prose inconsistencies with Table 3. These provide a modest reporting improvement while preserving the original empirical evidence; the proposed explanation for text-rendering failures remains untested.
